bds.h: Microsoft outage shows the risks of relying on a single technology provider for essential services
bds.lede: Microsoft said progress is being made in bringing its popular workplace software back online as a global outage enters its second day, disrupting business communications, police emergency calls, court operations and AI tools.
rows: Experts say outage exposes ‘Australia’s reliance on foreign technology’ as software giant says services being restored

Microsoft said progress is being made in bringing its popular workplace software back online as a global outage enters its second day, disrupting business communications, police emergency calls, court operations and AI tools.
Microsoft said server issues were behind the incident and that a broader rollout of software fixes was stabilizing the system.
Microsoft services began recovering on Friday after a global outage disrupted Outlook and Teams.
A Microsoft outage involving services like Outlook and Teams has impacted many users, companies and government services.

The company says it doesn’t have a timeline for a full recovery and blamed a “technical issue” for the outage, saying it was not the result of a cyberattack or artificial intelligence. NBC News’ Christine Romans reports.
